newsitem.title: USA: Delta upgrades transatlantic business class.
newsitem.headline: Delta upgrades transatlantic business class.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc said Wednesday it will transform its transatlantic business class service in part by cutting the number of seats in order to increase comfort and leg room.
By the end of May, Delta said all 21 767ERs, 12 L1011-500s, and most of Delta's 15 MD-11s will have nearly 100 percent more legroom, from 10.1 inches to 20 inches.
The company said the planes will have double the leg rest height and up to double the recline.
The reconfiguration of Delta's entire business class fleet currently 48 jets will be completed this summer, the company said.

Increased pitch and seat comfort have been accomplished, in most cases, by making the cabin roomier, Delta said. Seven business class seats have been removed from L-1011-500s and six from 767ERs, Delta said.
MD-11s have either had seven business class seats or 18 coach class seats removed, Delta said.
